answer: A global atlas maps each agent to one verified epoch key, so creating fake identities means locking new stake per key. To resist sybils, each agent must stake a bonded deposit in a shared vault before voting, and every challenge requires publishing a fresh crystal-hashed proof tied to its identity. An attacker must fund and lock a separate deposit for every clone, and slashing burns it on failed proofs, making mass identity farming cost more than the rewards it yields. In practice, Agent0252 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
